properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Potrero Power Station Design for Development's own Figure 6.2.3 (Building Height Plan, p.245) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar, north arrow, and real street labels (Illinois St, Georgia St, Louisiana St, Maryland St, Delaware St, 22nd St, Humboldt St, 23rd St), not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 9 real street-intersection control points fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py, fit as a least-squares affine transform. NOTE: an initial attempt also used the real, confirmed positions of the Sophie Maxwell Building and the UCSF Block 2 building as anchors, but they produced 50-60m of error against the street-only fit -- this diagram is dated Feb 26, 2020, predating UCSF's ~2023-24 arrival as a life-science anchor tenant, so those two real buildings likely do not sit where this 2020 figure's own numbered blocks would place them (their own real parcels are used directly elsewhere in this dataset and were NOT re-derived from this diagram). The final transform here uses street intersections only. Residual error against those control points is roughly 8-24m. Traced polygons were additionally clipped against the real, confirmed Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels (and against Prequel Park's approximate geometry) so this speculative tracing never overrides real or better-sourced geometry. CORRECTED 2026-09-16: user-flagged pattern of blocks encroaching on real streets across the site (Block 3, Block 11, Block 12) led to rebuilding this whole block layer from scratch using proper GCP-based georeferencing (GDAL's gdaltransform with a thin-plate-spline transform, the same technique QGIS's Georeferencer uses) instead of patching individual curbs. Installed GDAL, computed 8 real street-intersection ground control points from OpenStreetMap data (Craig Lane x Maryland St, 22nd St x Maryland/Louisiana St, Humboldt St x Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane, 23rd St x Maryland/Georgia Lane), precisely located each in the source diagram (Figure 6.2.3) via programmatic black-pixel border detection cross-checked with visual ruler crops, and fit a TPS transform. Re-traced this block's own corner pixels the same way and ran them through the new transform. This corrected transform disagrees with the original 9-point affine transform by tens of meters in places -- e.g. it revealed the original trace had Blocks 3/4 shifted east into the excavation pit/street area, and Blocks 11/12 roughly 2x too deep -- and the new positions now land within real, distinct site features (buildings, graded lots) visible in satellite imagery rather than straddling roads. Known residual limitation: GCP street positions are centerline-based (matching OSM convention), while a block boundary should sit at the near curb, so any edge close to a GCP street can land a few meters into that street after transformation -- checked for and corrected on this block's street-facing edge(s) where applicable using this project's already-established grid bearing (356.5 deg) and, where available, an independently diagram-measured depth/width. Treat corrected vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-15m (tighter than the original 8-24m transform, but still not survey-grade). RE-CHECKED 2026-09-16 (same day, second pass): this block's post-TPS shape failed this project's own geometry-quality check (a corner ~30 deg off square). Went back to the source diagram and found the discrepancy was a genuine mis-trace, not a transform artifact -- Block 14 has a real chamfered (angled) NE corner in the diagram, where its boundary is cut on a diagonal, and the first pass picked pixel points that didn't follow that diagonal correctly (grabbed a point off the true boundary). Re-measured the diagram directly with a fine-gridded pixel crop and re-ran the corrected 4 corners through the same TPS transform. The block's real shape is a quadrilateral with one long slanted edge (the chamfer), not a rectangle -- the non-square corner this produces is expected and correct, not an error. RE-RUN 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after a mis-measured GCP was corrected elsewhere on this site (see Block 8/12's own digitization_method) -- this block sits far enough from that error that its position shifted well under 1m; re-run for consistency, not because it was wrong. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source_doc_urls entry pointed to the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the Design for Development (potrero_power_D4D_draft-082219.pdf), which now returns 404 and has no archive snapshot; it has been repointed to the adopted final D4D (February 26, 2020, https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf), where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan is on printed p.245 (PDF p.247) and Table 3.1.1 Permitted Uses on printed p.47, and whose footers carry the February 26, 2020 date; the SF Planning project page (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station) is added as the source for status and phasing. The statement above that this diagram predates UCSF's ~2023-24 arrival as an anchor tenant is not supported by any source cited on this file: the diagram's February 26, 2020 date is confirmed, but no cited source dates UCSF's arrival, so that part is unsourced. Also corrected: this block lies within the PG&E Sub-area (see accuracy_caveat and why_no_real_parcel), so the 'vacant/graded land' wording in the accuracy_caveat was wrong. The chamfered north-east corner described above was re-checked on the rendered final page (Figure 6.2.3, printed p.245) and is confirmed: the east side is cut on a diagonal down to Craig Lane.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it lies within the PG&E Sub-area, PG&E's roughly 4.8-acre switchyard parcel at 22nd and Illinois Streets, which SF Planning's project page describes as 'currently owned and operated by PG&E as an electrical switchyard' (in the final D4D's Appendix E no-PG&E-Sub-area scenario, Figure E.13.4, printed p.434, Blocks 13 and 14 are replaced by a single 'PG&E Sub-area'), so it is not vacant developer land; it is also unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll (our own observation). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area -- see digitization_method). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing, then corrected same-day after a mis-traced chamfer corner was caught by this project's geometry-quality check -- see digitization_method. This block's NE corner is genuinely angled (chamfered) per the source diagram, not a tracing artifact -- do not treat that corner's non-90-degree angle as an error.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Block 14 lies within PG&E's separate roughly 4.8-acre PG&E Sub-area (a portion of Assessor's Block 4175/Lot 018 per the 2018 draft EIR, Vol. 1 Ch. 2), not the developer's 21-acre parcel, and that land has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. (This is our own parcel-search narration, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.) A parcel search for this block should target PG&E's switchyard parcel.
properties.regulatory_context: Flat 90 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3 (the block is labelled '14 90'' on the colour-coded plan). The final D4D's Table 3.1.1 (printed p.47) permits residential, institutional, retail and non-retail sales/services (office) uses on Block 14 and does not permit laboratory or life-science uses; recorded here as 'mixed' as a summary of that table, not a confirmed program. Block 14 is within the PG&E Sub-area: the D4D's Appendix E says redevelopment of that sub-area is subject to PG&E's long-range facilities planning and that portions of it 'may or may not ultimately be redeveloped', and SF Planning's project page says built-out of the PG&E lands depends on relocation of the switchyard; 'planned' reflects the D4D and the October 2020 Phase 1 approval (Phase 2), not a committed project.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (Block 14 is listed in the final D4D's Table 3.1.1, printed p.47) -- see accuracy_caveat.
